title: Minimum Wage Increases and Employer Performance: Role of Employer Heterogeneity
eligible_reason: Treatment is continuous, not binary. Every regression in Tables_MSsubmission.do uses Lmax_mw (log of the maximum of state and federal minimum wage, Vaghul-Zipperer series) as the regressor of interest (Tables 2, 4, 5, 6, 8; Table 3 border-county-pair design; Table 7 uses lagged Lmax_mw on county entry rates). No 0/1 adoption indicator is constructed anywhere. In addition, all specifications include time-varying county and hotel controls, and the preferred specifications add state-specific linear trends (absorb(cornellid year c.trend#stateid)). Fails the binary-treatment rule, so not a near-miss either.
design_notes: Hotel-year panel 2000-2008 (STR census, ~29,000 hotels). Table 2: reghdfe LADR/occrate/Lrevpar on Lmax_mw + controls, three FE sets: (i) cornellid year c.trend#stateid, cluster cornellid; (ii) stateid year, cluster stateid; (iii) cornellid year, cluster cornellid. Table 3: contiguous border county pairs, absorb(pair_id_real#year cornellid). Tables 4-6, 8: subsample splits by segment, organizational form, right-to-work. Table 7: county-year entry rates on L.Lmax_mw with county and year FE. Continuous-treatment generalized DiD (Cengiz et al. cited per flags) but no binary event.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Minimum wage changes are staggered across states and years but enter as a continuous log level; no binary cohorts defined.
